name: Brightpick Autopicker
summary: A wheeled warehouse robot with a lifting mast and a picking arm that pulls storage totes from shelving and picks items up to 2.5 kg into order totes, sold as a complete system of at least 10 to 15 robots.

germany.statusNote: Sold as a full installation (robots, software, shelving, installation) by the maker, whose R&D and manufacturing base is in Bratislava; running at Dr. Max in Prague and Brightpick robots run at Knuspr in Munich. No public euro price; no single robots.

priceOther.market: Robots-as-a-Service per robot per month, 3-year term, plus USD 1,000 implementation fee per robot (min. USD 70k); Brightpick pricing page as served to this check

germany.leadTime: 4-7 months from order to installation, then 3-4 weeks on-site installation (maker FAQ)

sellers.name: Brightpick s.r.o.
sellers.note: European base in Bratislava (Plynarenska 6); sells and installs directly with its own installation team, RaaS or purchase.

specs.label: Minimum clear height
specs.conditions: needed by the robot, e.g. in mezzanines

specs.label: Heaviest item it picks
specs.conditions: heavier items go to a goods-to-person station for a human picker

specs.label: Runtime
specs.conditions: full battery, up to; 1 h charging gives 6 h of work; robots charge themselves

specs.label: Floor flatness
specs.value: max. 10 mm per m (shelving up to 3.5 m), 6 mm per m above 3.5 m

specs.label: Sensors
specs.value: LiDARs and 3D vision; SLAM navigation without floor markers

specs.label: Integration
specs.value: APIs to the customer WMS/ERP; Brightpick Intuition fleet software

specs.label: Minimum order
specs.value: 15 robots per installation (pricing page); FAQ says smallest deployment starts at 10 robots

capabilities.sdk: WMS/ERP integration via Brightpick APIs; no open robot SDK found
notes: Works only inside its own shelving system on flat warehouse floors (max. 10 mm per m deviation); new racks are usually recommended.
Picks single items up to 2.5 kg; heavier items are brought to a human at a goods-to-person station.
Not sold as a single robot: complete installations only, at least 10 to 15 robots.
Not for frozen storage. The type of end effector (suction or fingers) is not stated on the pages opened.
roughGround and stairs set to false because the maker states floor flatness limits and the robot runs in shelving aisles.

images.alt: Two Brightpick Autopicker robots with blue totes in the shelving aisles of the Dr. Max warehouse in Prague

evidence.task: Picks slow-moving pharmacy items, replenishes stock and re-slots totes in a distribution centre; 30 Autopickers pick about 20,000 items per day
evidence.where: Dr. Max distribution centre, Prague, Czech Republic
evidence.note: 9 robots from late 2023, 21 more in 2025 and 2026.

evidence.task: Robotic picking of all 2,500 SKUs in the ambient zone of an e-grocery fulfilment centre, designed for 600 picks per hour
evidence.where: Rohlik Group fulfilment centre, Prague, Czech Republic
evidence.note: The article describes Brightpick robotic picking; it does not name the robot model in the lines checked.

evidence.task: Kitting and parts supply for manufacturers' fulfilment
evidence.note: Industrial page of the maker; no construction customer found.

openQuestions: Euro price for Germany: the pricing page shows USD 2,190 per robot per month, the FAQ says from USD 1,990 in the U.S.; no EUR price found.
Minimum order: 15 robots on the pricing and Autopicker pages vs. 10 robots in the FAQ.
The Munich (Knuspr) installation uses Brightpick Dispatcher robots, not Autopickers; no Autopicker site in Germany was found.
End effector type, robot dimensions, speed and CE/safety certificates are not on the pages opened.
